He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso Crusaders]], where he was named an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 2012. He represented the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] on multiple occasions. ==Early life== Broekhoff was born in [[Melbourne]], [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]], in the suburb of [[Frankston, Victoria|Frankston]].{{cite web |title=Ryan Broekhoff |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/75869/sid/8054/tid/239/tid2/_/2015_FIBA_Oceania_Championship/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=1 December 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101160314/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/75869/sid/8054/tid/239/tid2/_/2015_FIBA_Oceania_Championship/index.html |archive-date=1 November 2015}} He grew up playing for the [[Frankston Blues]] as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/family-first-for-broekhoff|title=Family First for Broekhoff|website=semphoenix.com.au|date=12 July 2023|access-date=12 July 2023}} He attended [[The Peninsula School]] in Melbourne.{{cite web| title=#45 – Ryan Broekhoff | work = ValpoAthletics.com | url =http://www.valpoathletics.com/mbasketball/roster/2012-13/5983/ryan-broekhoff/ | access-date = 8 March 2014}} In 2008 and 2009, he played in the [[South East Australian Basketball League]] (SEABL) for the [[BA Centre of Excellence|Australian Institute of Sport]].{{cite web|url=https://websites.mygameday.app/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=194501570&client=0-3363-150604-148538-4362809|title=Player statistics for Ryan Broekhoff|website=SEABL|access-date=12 July 2023}}{{cite web|url=http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes |title=Past Athletes |work=ausport.gov.au |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140212073754/http://www.ausport.gov.au/ais/sports/basketball/athletes/past_athletes |archive-date=12 February 2014}} ==College career== Broekhoff played four years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso Crusaders]] between 2009 and 2013. After playing a support role as a freshman in [[2009–10 Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball team|2009–10]], Broekhoff entered the starting line-up as a sophomore, averaging 10.3 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. He led the [[Horizon League]] in [[three-point field goal]] percentage at 44.8% and placed sixth in the conference in [[blocked shot]]s with 1.1 per contest. As a junior in [[2011–12 Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball team|2011–12]], Broekhoff became one of the top players in the Horizon League. He averaged 14.8 points, 8.6 rebounds (first in the Horizon League) and 2.3 assists per game and led the Crusaders to the conference regular-season title and a [[National Invitation Tournament]] bid. At the end of the season, he was named [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Player of the Year]]{{cite web| title=Broekhoff Named HL Player of the Year; Drew Coach of the Year | publisher = Valparaiso University | year = 2012 | url =http://www.valpoathletics.com/mbasketball/news-print/2011-12/11497/broekhoff-named-hl-player-of-the-year-drew-coach-of-the-year/ | access-date = 8 August 2012}} and an honourable mention [[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]].{{cite web | title = Broekhoff Named AP Honorable Mention All-American | publisher = Valparaiso University | year = 2012 | url = http://valpo.streamlinetechnologies.com/mbasketball/news/2011-12/11591/broekhoff-named-ap-honorable-mention-all-american/ | access-date = 8 August 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140108121031/http://valpo.streamlinetechnologies.com/mbasketball/news/2011-12/11591/broekhoff-named-ap-honorable-mention-all-american/ | archive-date = 8 January 2014 | df = dmy-all }} As a senior in [[2012–13 Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball team|2012–13]], Broekhoff averaged 15.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 32.2 minutes per game. He led his team to a 26–7 record and the top seed in the Horizon League tournament. In the semi-final game against Green Bay-Wisconsin, he hit the game-winning shot to send Valparaiso to the title game. The Crusaders won the title game against Wright State and clinched an NCAA Tournament berth, where they lost in the first game. ==Professional career== ===Turkey and Russia (2013–2018)=== Between 2013 and 2015, Broekhoff played for [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball League]] (TBL).[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/104634/ryan-broekhoff-inks-with-besiktas.html Ryan Broekhoff inks with Besiktas][https://web.archive.org/web/20130812013001/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2013-14/i/115257/8174/besiktas-lands-aussie-rookie-broekhoff BESIKTAS lands Aussie rookie Broekhoff][http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/173721/besiktas-officially-parted-ways-with-ryan-broekhoff.html Besiktas officially parted ways with Ryan Broekhoff] Broekhoff played for the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].[http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/sports/ct-ptb-local-roundup-st-0710-20150709-story.html Local Roundup: Ryan Broekhoff to play for Denver Nuggets in NBA Summer League] Between 2015 and 2018, Broekhoff played for [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{cite web|title=Lokomotiv Kuban signs Ryan Broekhoff to a three-year deal|url=https://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/175115/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-ryan-broekhoff-to-a-three-year-deal.html|date=6 September 2015|website=sportando.com|access-date=6 September 2015}} In 16 VTB United League games in 2017–18, he averaged 8.1 points, 4.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 steals per game. In 16 EuroCup games, he averaged 12.3 points, 5.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists en route to earning [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup First Team]] honours.{{cite web |title=Mavericks sign Ryan Broekhoff |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-ryan-broekhoff/ |work=Mavs.com |access-date=6 August 2018 |date=6 August 2018}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2018–2020)=== On 6 August 2018, Broekhoff signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He played in 42 games during the [[2018–19 NBA season]].{{cite web |title=Ryan Broekhoff 2018-19 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/broekry01/gamelog/2019 |work=basketball-reference.com |access-date=12 July 2023}} On 23 March 2019, he scored a season-high 17 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He returned to the Mavericks for the [[2019–20 NBA season]], but was waived on 11 February 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mkgsigning/|title=Mavs ink Michael Kidd-Gilchrist; he'll wear No. 9 for Dallas|date=11 February 2020|publisher=mavs.com|access-date=11 February 2020}} He played in 17 games in his second season.{{cite web |title=Ryan Broekhoff 2019-20 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/broekry01/gamelog/2020 |work=basketball-reference.com |access-date=12 July 2023}} Broekhoff initially signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in June 2020 for the NBA's 2019–20 season restart,{{cite web|title=Team Signs Broekhoff|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-broekhoff|date=27 June 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=27 June 2020}} but ultimately did not join the team in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando bubble]].{{cite web|title=76ers' Ryan Broekhoff: Won't join Sixers in bubble|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-ryan-broekhoff-wont-join-sixers-in-bubble/|date=21 July 2020|website=cbssports.com|access-date=12 July 2023}} He re-joined the 76ers in November 2020{{cite web|title=76ers' Ryan Broekhoff: Rejoins Sixers|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-ryan-broekhoff-rejoins-sixers/|date=24 November 2020|website=cbssports.com|access-date=12 July 2023}} but was released after training camp in mid December prior to the start of the [[2020–21 NBA season]].{{cite web|title=Ryan Broekhoff: Let go by Sixers|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/ryan-broekhoff-let-go-by-sixers/|date=14 December 2020|website=cbssports.com|access-date=12 July 2023}}{{Cite web|title=Ryan Broekhoff: Finds opportunity Down Under|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/ryan-broekhoff-finds-opportunity-down-under/|access-date=25 April 2021|website=CBSSports.com|date=15 February 2021}} ===South East Melbourne Phoenix (2021–2023)=== On 15 February 2021, Broekhoff signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] for the remainder of the [[2020–21 NBL season]].{{cite web|title=Ryan Broekhoff Signs with South East Melbourne|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/ryan-broekhoff-signs-with-south-east-melbourne|date=15 February 2021|website=NBL.com.au|access-date=15 February 2021}} He averaged 7.5 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Ryan Broekhoff |url=https://nbl.com.au/player/113805/1640134/ryan-broekhoff |website=NBL |access-date=15 June 2021}} On 28 June 2021, Broekhoff re-signed with the Phoenix on a two-year contract.{{cite web |title=Broekhoff Back with the Phoenix |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/broekhoff-back-with-the-phoenix |date=28 June 2021 |website=NBL |access-date=28 June 2021}} He sustained a shoulder injury in March 2022 that ruled him out for four weeks.{{cite web |title=Deep Heat Injury Update – Ryan Broekhoff |url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/deep-heat-injury-update-ryan-broekhoff |date=15 March 2022 |website=semphoenix.com.au |access-date=15 March 2022}} A hip complaint kept Broekhoff out for an extended period early in the [[2022–23 NBL season]], and in January 2023, he suffered a groin injury that ruled him out for the rest of the regular season.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/season-could-be-over-for-broekhoff|title=Season Could Be Over for Broekhoff|work=NBL.com.au|date=22 January 2023|access-date=23 January 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/hooley-concerned-for-phoenix-following-broekhoff-injury|title=Hooley "Concerned" For Phoenix Following Broekhoff Injury|work=NBL.com.au|date=23 January 2023|access-date=23 January 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/broekhoff-out-2-3-weeks|title=Broekhoff Out 2-3 Weeks|work=NBL.com.au|date=24 January 2023|access-date=24 January 2023}}{{cite web|last=Woods|first=Dan|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/broekhoff-fighting-fit-for-play-in-qualifier|title=Broekhoff Fighting Fit for Play-In Qualifier|website=NBL.com.au|date=8 February 2023|access-date=8 February 2023}} On 12 July 2023, Broekhoff announced his retirement from basketball.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/broekhoff-calls-time-on-illustrious-career|title=Broekhoff Calls Time On Illustrious Career|website=NBL.com.au|date=12 July 2023|access-date=12 July 2023}} ==National team career== Broekhoff was a member of Australia's entry in both the [[2009 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] in [[Auckland]], New Zealand, and the [[Basketball at the 2011 Summer Universiade|2011 Summer Universiade]] in [[Shenzhen]], China. He continued his career with the national basketball program in 2012 as he was invited to the trials for the Australia's [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|2012 London Olympic]] team. Broekhoff was one of the last cuts on the squad, making the final 14 before being released.{{cite web| title=BOOMERS ARRIVE IN MELBOURNE FOR CAMP | work = Basketball.net.au | date = 19 June 2012 | url =http://www.basketball.net.au/boomers-arrive-in-melbourne-for-camp/ | access-date = 8 August 2012}} In 2013, Broekhoff competed in the 2013 Stanković Cup and World University Games, winning gold and silver, respectively.{{cite web | url=http://www.unisport.com.au/News/Pages/EmergingBoomerswinSilver.aspx | title=Emerging Boomers win Silver | work=UniSport.com.au | date=12 July 2013 | access-date=4 March 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304145550/http://www.unisport.com.au/News/Pages/EmergingBoomerswinSilver.aspx | archive-date=4 March 2014 | df=dmy-all }} In August 2013, he was named in the Boomers' [[2013 FIBA Oceania Championship]] squad to take on New Zealand in a two-game series.{{cite web | url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/australian-boomers-team-named-for-fiba-world-cup-20140728-zxhdm.html | title=AUSTRALIAN BOOMERS TEAM NAMED FOR FIBA WORLD CUP | work=The Sydney Morning Herald | date=27 July 2014 | access-date=18 August 2015}} He impressed coach [[Andrej Lemanis]] during several warm-up games{{cite news | url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/basketball/australian-boomers-win-world-cup-warmup-against-ukraine-in-nice/news-story/319e33e3774ea77ce3c616778442ef00 | title=Australian Boomers win World Cup during the tournament.{{cite web | url=http://www.sportal.com.au/nba/dante-exum-tipped-to-shine/13wf0mrl3wk7y1m0q37uuxc725 | title=DANTE EXUM TIPPED TO SHINE | work=sportal.com.au | date=28 August archive-date=24 September 2015 | df=dmy-all }} Broekhoff returned to the Boomers' starting line-up for the two-game [[2015 FIBA Oceania Championship|FIBA Oceania Championship]] series against New Zealand in August 2015.{{cite web | url=http://www.fibalivestats.com/matches/151/16/15/21/79M0s8CnScXvg/ | title=Australia vs New Zealand | work=FIBALiveStats.com | date=15 August 2015 |
